sections.h2: Where are Texas property records kept?
sections.html:
Deeds and related instruments are recorded by the county clerk in the county where the real property is located. The Texas courts' county clerk manual describes the clerk as the county recorder, alongside duties as clerk of the commissioners court and keeper of probate filings.

That means a house in one county is searched in that county's records, even if the owner lives somewhere else. Texas has 254 counties, according to the Comptroller, and each clerk runs its own index and search system. Some offer online search and some require a visit, so ask the clerk's office how its records can be searched.

sections.h2: Which documents get recorded in the deed records?
sections.html:
The clerk manual lists general warranty deeds, special warranty deeds, quitclaim deeds, trustee's deeds, sheriff's deeds and tax deeds among the instruments filed there. Affidavits, releases of deeds of trust, leases, contracts of sale and powers of attorney go in the same records.

  • Deeds that move ownership from one party to another.
  • Deeds of trust that secure a mortgage, and the releases that cancel them.
  • Notices of foreclosure sale, which the clerk files before a lender's auction.
  • State tax lien notices, which the Comptroller files with the clerk for entry in the state tax lien book.
  • Probate papers that carry title, such as a muniment order or a recorded affidavit of death for a transfer on death deed.

Everything in that list shows up in a title search, which is why a clean record matters when a house is listed.

sections.h2: What makes a Texas deed ready to record?
sections.html:
The instrument has to be signed and acknowledged, or sworn to before two subscribing witnesses. The county clerk manual cites Property Code section 12.001(b) for this rule and names notaries, clerks and county court judges among the officers who can take an acknowledgment.

A deed that lacks the acknowledgment can be turned away, and a missing grantee mailing address can add a fee. Check the names on the deed against the names in the prior recorded deed, because a mismatch creates questions at closing. A title company or attorney usually prepares the deed so these details are caught early.

sections.h2: What does recording cost in a Texas county clerk's office?
sections.html:
The base fee is set by statute and printed in the clerk manual, and counties add smaller charges on top. The table below reproduces the figures from the 2023 manual.

County clerk recording fees printed in the Texas courts' 2023 clerk manual
ItemAmount printed
First page$5.00
Each additional page, part of a page or attachment$4.00
Each name over five to be indexed$0.25
Records management and preservation feeNot more than $10
Records archive feeNot more than $10
Records technology and infrastructure fee$2.00
Notice of foreclosure sale filing$2.00 per notice

The manual also notes that a commissioners court may direct the clerk to waive real property recording fees for buyers using certain federal or state grant programs. The current schedule is on the county clerk's website or at the counter, since fees are updated from time to time.

sections.h2: Does Texas charge a transfer tax when a deed is recorded?
sections.html:
The clerk manual and Comptroller pages describe recording fees only, and no state transfer or documentary stamp tax appears on them. Ask the county clerk or a title company to confirm the full list of charges for your closing.

Property tax is a separate matter. The tax lien for each year attaches on January 1, and the owner on that date is liable for the year's tax even after a sale, as the Comptroller explains. That is why the closing statement splits the year's tax between seller and buyer, and why a title search checks for unpaid years.

sections.h2: How do liens show up in Texas property records?
sections.html:
Mortgage liens appear as recorded deeds of trust, and a release is recorded when the loan is paid off. If a payoff was never released on paper, the old deed of trust can still show on a title search and may need a release before closing.

Tax liens work differently. A property tax lien attaches automatically on January 1 and secures that year's tax, penalties and interest, and state tax liens are recorded by the Comptroller with the county clerk. Tax foreclosure deeds are also filed with the clerk. Because liens can follow the property, a buyer's title company will run a search before it issues a policy.

  • Deeds of trust and their releases.
  • Unpaid property tax for any year.
  • State tax lien notices in the lien book.
  • Judgment or contractor claims, where the clerk's index shows them.

sections.h2: What records matter after a death or a foreclosure?
sections.html:
After a death, the recorded document that carries title changes with the route used. The State Law Library says an administered estate needs an executor's or administrator's deed, a muniment of title needs the court order and will, and a transfer on death deed needs an affidavit of death and the death certificate. The clerk cannot add heirs to an older deed.

Foreclosure leaves its own trail. A lender's notice of sale is posted at the courthouse door and filed with the county clerk at least 21 days before the sale, and the commissioners court designates where in the county sales take place, recorded in the real property records. Sales run between 10 a.m. and 4 p.m. on the first Tuesday of the month, per the Attorney General's guidance. A trustee's deed after the sale is recorded the same way as other deeds.

sections.h2: How can a seller check the records before listing?
sections.html:
Pull the recent deed and any open deed of trust, confirm the names match, and ask the county clerk or a title company for a search. A seller who finds a problem early has more time to fix it.

  • Match the owner's name on the deed to the name on the listing.
  • Find the deed of trust and confirm the loan balance or release.
  • Check the appraisal district for the owner of record and any exemptions.
  • Ask whether any state tax lien notice is filed.
  • For an inherited house, confirm the probate document is recorded in the right county.

faqs.q: Who keeps property records in Texas?
faqs.a: The county clerk of the county where the property sits. The clerk acts as county recorder and files deeds, deeds of trust, releases, liens and foreclosure sale notices.

faqs.q: How much does it cost to record a deed in Texas?
faqs.a: The 2023 county clerk manual prints $5.00 for the first page and $4.00 for each additional page, plus other capped or fixed county fees. Check the clerk's current schedule for the exact total.

faqs.q: What does a Texas deed need before it can be recorded?
faqs.a: It must be signed and acknowledged, or sworn before two subscribing witnesses. A notary or another authorized officer can take the acknowledgment.

faqs.q: Can the county clerk add heirs to an old deed?
faqs.a: No. After a death, a new instrument such as an executor's deed, a muniment order or an affidavit of death has to be recorded instead.

faqs.q: Where do foreclosure notices get filed?
faqs.a: With the county clerk, and they are also posted at the courthouse door at least 21 days before the sale. The clerk manual lists a $2.00 fee per notice.
